title: balance.json still ships the removed budget's default_budget key; no code reads it
detail: The budget was replaced by the hardware tray (ruling 0b92fa4), but the dead tunable still ships in the single-source data file. The loader silently ignores unknown keys, so it loads unnoticed and misleads editors into thinking a budget exists.
recommended_fix: Delete the default_budget key from balance.json; starting_inventory and grants are the replacement economy.

title: Pipe_Tier.cost_per_tile is a budget-era cost model orphaned by the tray ruling
evidence:
core/catalog.odin:33: 	cost_per_tile:  i32,
data/pipe_tiers.json:2: "_comment": "... cost_per_tile = draw cost factor (cost = length x cost_per_tile). ..."
data/pipe_tiers.json:10:       "cost_per_tile": 5,
detail: cost_per_tile is parsed into Pipe_Tier but no proc in core, app, or harness ever reads it (grep: catalog.odin only). The catalog comment still documents the cost formula, so editors believe cost gates draws when the tray economy prices nothing.
recommended_fix: Remove cost_per_tile from Pipe_Tier and pipe_tiers.json, and drop the cost-formula comment; reintroduce with a real economy later.

title: draw_and_upgrade.dem header still claims demolish refunds into the removed budget
evidence: # over-span upgrade rejection (Perkins r1), demolish refunds into the budget.
detail: The demo header documents demolish refunding into the budget, but the ruling replaced it with the tray: remove_pipe returns the link to inventory (core/topology.odin). draw_and_reject.dem was the r1-reported stale header; this second header still carries the same claim.
recommended_fix: Reword to 'demolish refunds the link into the tray'.

title: HUD header comment still lists budget among the chrome elements
evidence: // SLA chips, budget, forecast ("weather report"), alerts, and the win/lose
detail: The HUD now draws the hardware tray (draw_tray reads snapshot inv_links/inv_routers), but the file's header comment still names the budget. Stale doc from the pre-ruling era.

title: project-context.md still instructs agents that game/ is the reference build; game/ no longer exists
evidence: - **Reference build:** `game/` is the frozen Godot prototype — behavioral reference only; never ported line-by-line, never extended.
detail: The Odin pivot removed game/ from the tree (no game/ dir at the worktree root; commit 0df9135), but the live conventions doc still tells agents game/ is the behavioral reference. The guidance is unfollowable; only git history holds the prototype.
recommended_fix: Point the reference at the frozen git tag (prototype-fun-gate) or delete the line.

title: demand.json root growth_roles is never read; balance.json's copy is the only source
evidence:
data/demand.json:65:   "growth_roles": [
core/catalog.odin:435: 	if gr, okg := obj["growth_roles"].(json.Array); okg {  // in the BALANCE block only
detail: catalogs_load reads growth_roles only from balance.json (7 residentials); demand.json's root copy (4 residentials) is never parsed. A second source of truth that silently does nothing when edited, and its count already diverges from balance.json.
recommended_fix: Delete demand.json's growth_roles block, or have the loader cross-check it against balance.json.

title: Unknown terminal-role strings in demand entries silently become .None — no fail-fast, unlike node_types
detail: A typo'd source_role/sink_role in demand.json passes load and the entry's traffic becomes permanent E28 droppage (no terminal matches .None), while node_types fails fast on the identical .None condition. Violates the file header's 'out-of-range values abort with a named error' claim.
recommended_fix: Reject .None roles for demand source_role/sink_role at load, mirroring the node_types check.

title: Init-time arrays allocate on the caller's heap, step grows them under the run arena — per-restart leaks; run_destroy dead
detail: Init-time appends (flow sla/roll arrays, director flags, growth_pool, bootstrap topology) use the caller's heap; step grows them under the run arena, so heap blocks are never freed — every restart/demo leaks. run_destroy, called nowhere, frees only the two id maps.
recommended_fix: Pass the run allocator explicitly through flow_init/director_init_growth/run_init_bare (or set context.allocator there), and free inventory/flow arrays in run_destroy or remove it.

title: compute_route silently drops valid paths of 33+ pipes as unroutable (E28)
evidence:
core/flow.odin:16: MAX_ROUTE :: 32          // max pipes along a packet's path (nodes <= 64 in PROTO)
core/flow.odin:256: 		if i >= MAX_ROUTE { p.route_len = 0; return }
detail: A valid shortest path of 33+ pipes returns route_len 0, so the packet never spawns and demand accrues as E28 Unreachable loss though a path exists. The cap's own comment admits ≤64-node topologies, where 33+ hop chains are possible.
recommended_fix: Raise MAX_ROUTE to cover 64-node paths, or return a distinct routing error instead of a silent Unreachable drop.
